plot: The night after the rescue, the kitten Button sleeps in the Dough Bros' own bread basket and jealous Bup wants her gone, especially when Mom says she goes to a farm on Monday if she cries all night again; Lolly lures her with a sock into a cozy shoebox, but she cries louder than ever and Dad's footsteps head for the stairs — the twist: Zeek's note that she went silent at 2 a.m. last night (exactly when the bros lay down beside her, said at the start) means she wasn't crying for the basket but for them, her new littermates; jealous Bup climbs in first, all five sleep in a pile, Button stays — then Mia brings in a lamppost poster: LOST, grey kitten, answers to Smoke.

script.title: Why Won't the Kitten Leave Our Bed?

beats.say: Hey! That's my pillow! A kitten just kicked me out of bed!
Our basket, Bup. Our bed. And she's snoring in it!
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Midnight in the kitchen. The kitten Pim saved now has a name.
Mia named her Button. And Mom gave her the bros' bread basket.
Mia said goodnight to Button. Three times. She forgot us.
She didn't forget us. She just didn't look at us.
Can we sleep on the towel? Far, far away from claws?
Data first. Last night Button cried for three straight hours.
Then at two a.m., total silence. I wrote it down.
Two a.m. That's when we lay down on the towel beside her.
Who cares when she stopped crying? She's sleeping in our bed!
Bup marches up to the basket. Button opens one sleepy eye.
Polite first. Excuse me, miss. You're lying on our blanket.
Button yawns. Then she stretches all four paws. Even wider.
I said, EXCUSE ME!
Upstairs, a door clicks. Mom's slippers shuffle down the stairs.
The bros freeze like crumbs. Mom peeks into the basket.
She whispers into her phone to Dad, who is still in bed.
If she cries all night again, she goes to a farm Monday.
The farm? She's a baby! She can't live on a farm!
Or maybe that fixes everything. She goes. We get our bed.
Bup! Tell me you don't mean that.
Maybe I do. A little. Mia was ours first.
Mom goes back up. The kitchen is dark and quiet again.
Lolly drags one of Dad's old socks from the laundry pile.
We move her gently, to a cozy shoebox. Everybody wins.
Shoebox. Soft lining. Right beside the warm fridge. Acceptable.
Lolly wiggles the sock. Button's eyes go huge. She pounces!
Sock, kitten, sock, kitten, all the way across the floor.
Into the shoebox. Button sniffs the sock. Lolly tiptoes back.
It worked? It worked! And nobody got scratched!
Five seconds later, the crying starts. Loud. Louder than ever.
That is not a sleepy cry. That is a lonely one.
Upstairs, Dad's bed creaks. Heavy footsteps head for the stairs.
If Dad hears this, Button leaves on Monday. Somebody think!
Wait. Zeek. Say the two a.m. thing again.
She cried for hours. Then silence at two. So what?
So at two, all five of us lay right next to her.
She wasn't crying for the basket. She was crying for us.
Kittens sleep in a pile with their brothers and sisters.
She lost hers out there. So she picked the next best family.
Bup runs to the shoebox and climbs right in beside Button.
Okay, okay. I'm here. Big brother's here. Shh.
The crying stops. Button curls around Bup like a warm scarf.
On the stairs, Dad stops. Listens. Nothing. He goes back to bed.
Can I come in too? If nobody has their claws out?
One by one, all five climb into the box. Even Crispy.
She's purring. Something is purring at me. That's new.
Sunday morning. Mia finds one kitten and five bros, fast asleep.
Mom texts Dad. Slept all night. Button stays. Mia squeals.
Bup, yesterday you wanted her gone. And she chose you.
Mia was ours first. Now we're Button's first. Fair's fair.
Then Mia runs in from the street, holding a crumpled paper.
A poster from the lamppost. Lost: grey kitten. Answers to Smoke.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
